title: Jira mandates Supabase; production runs Firebase
claim: REL-201 mandates Supabase for every v2 service, but dozens of production commits since June write to Firebase—and a 2am Slack thread admits the migration was abandoned to hit launch.
engineHint: The Supabase mandate predates the Firebase commits by six months. The Slack admission explicitly ties the pivot to the launch deadline.

evidence.author: Priya Raman
evidence.quote: REL-201: All v2 services must use Supabase. Firebase is explicitly out of scope for the platform roadmap.

evidence.author: Marcus Webb
evidence.quote: feat(api): move orders + auth to Firestore; remove Supabase client

evidence.author: Dani Okafor
evidence.quote: We are not going to finish the Supabase migration before launch. I moved the remaining services to Firebase last night. Please do not put this in writing yet.

evidence.author: Marcus Webb
evidence.quote: const db = getFirestore(app); // Supabase migration deferred until Q4

resolutions.label: Firebase is canonical
resolutions.description: Ratify the production reality and rewrite the architecture mandate.

resolutions.label: Supabase is canonical
resolutions.description: Reopen the migration and scope a Firebase rollback.

resolutions.label: Dual-write, document both
resolutions.description: Keep Firebase live and document a time-boxed Supabase migration.

title: Ghost cron exports customer data to a personal bucket
claim: A nightly customer export runs with no documented owner or alerting—and the only routing note points to the outgoing engineer’s personal AWS bucket.
engineHint: The runbook names the Data Platform team, but the cron target was changed last November and never reverted.

evidence.author: Priya Raman
evidence.quote: Nightly customer export writes to s3://relay-prod-exports and is owned by the Data Platform team.

evidence.author: Tobias Klein
evidence.quote: 0 2 * * * /opt/relay/bin/export_customers.sh --bucket s3://tklein-personal-exports

evidence.author: Tobias Klein
evidence.quote: I pointed the export at my own bucket while I debug the retention job. I am leaving Friday—someone should probably take this over.

evidence.author: Nadia Chen
evidence.quote: Does anyone own the 2am export? It failed three nights in a row and nobody got paged.

resolutions.label: Take ownership + rotate bucket
resolutions.description: Move exports back to the company S3 bucket and assign an owner.

resolutions.label: Decommission the export
resolutions.description: Confirm no consumers, then remove the cron and the bucket.

resolutions.label: Escalate to security
resolutions.description: Treat the personal bucket as a potential data-exfiltration incident.

title: Security handbook says KMS; config ships a hardcoded password
claim: The security handbook says all secrets live in AWS KMS, but the staging API ships a hardcoded database password—and an intern flagged it in Slack two weeks ago.
engineHint: The hardcoded value matches the staging password in the runbook. SEC-88 was closed as Done without a linked PR or deploy.

evidence.author: Priya Raman
evidence.quote: All production and staging secrets are stored in AWS KMS. No credentials may be committed to source control.

evidence.author: Dani Okafor
evidence.quote: const DB_PASSWORD =

evidence.author: Iris Park
evidence.quote: I found a database password in config.ts while onboarding. Is that supposed to be there? It matches the staging runbook.

evidence.author: Nadia Chen
evidence.quote: SEC-88 marked Done: “migrate staging secrets to KMS.” No linked PR or deploy found.

resolutions.label: Rotate + move to KMS now
resolutions.description: Rotate the staging credential, purge git history, and finish the KMS migration.

resolutions.label: Rotate only, document exception

resolutions.label: Escalate as an incident
resolutions.description: Open a security incident and freeze the release until remediated.

title: Billing runbook promises 5 retries; handler ships 3
claim: The billing runbook promises five retries with exponential backoff, but the deployed Stripe handler uses three fixed-delay retries—and the discrepancy landed after PR #412.
engineHint: The runbook predates the handler refactor. The code comment marks the change as temporary.

evidence.author: Maya Chen
evidence.quote: Webhook failures retry 5 times with exponential backoff (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 12h).

evidence.author: Sam Ortiz
evidence.quote: MAX_RETRIES = 3; RETRY_DELAY_MS = 60_000  # simplified, backoff dropped for now

evidence.author: Maya Chen
evidence.quote: Are we still seeing failed renewals? Finance says a few accounts went dark after the Stripe outage.

evidence.author: Maya Chen
evidence.quote: BILL-77: Finance reports three renewals missing after the Stripe outage. Still investigating retry behavior.

resolutions.label: Restore 5x backoff
resolutions.description: Revert to the documented retry policy and replay missed events.

resolutions.label: Update runbook to 3x
resolutions.description: Accept the simplified handler and correct the documentation.

resolutions.label: Needs a billing decision
resolutions.description: Escalate to finance and the incoming owner before changing behavior.

title: Three Node versions across CI, engines, and onboarding
claim: CI pins Node 18, package.json requires Node 20, and the onboarding guide tells new hires to install Node 22—so every environment disagrees.
engineHint: Three sources, three versions. package.json is enforced at install time; CI is the oldest reference.

evidence.author: CI Bot
evidence.quote: node-version: 18.x

evidence.author: Sam Ortiz
evidence.quote: "engines": { "node": ">=20" }

evidence.author: Maya Chen
evidence.quote: Install Node 22 before running the dev server. Node 18 is no longer supported.

evidence.author: Iris Park
evidence.quote: My first build failed on Node 18. The onboarding doc said 22, CI says 18. Which one is real?

resolutions.label: Standardise on Node 22
resolutions.description: Bump CI and engines; keep onboarding as the source of truth.

resolutions.label: Standardise on Node 20
resolutions.description: Align CI and onboarding to the current LTS.

resolutions.label: Pin all three, document matrix
resolutions.description: Support a tested version matrix and remove ambiguity.

title: v2 rollback plan referenced but never written
claim: The v2 release notes claim a rollback plan is in place, but no runbook, script, or owner exists—and Slack shows the on-call engineer cannot find it.
engineHint: Referenced in the release email and Slack; no linked document or script exists in the repo.

evidence.author: Priya Raman
evidence.quote: Rollback plan is in place, see the release checklist before we cut v2.

evidence.author: Dev Patel
evidence.quote: Which checklist? I cannot find a rollback section anywhere. We do not have a script for this.

evidence.author: CI Bot
evidence.quote: No files matched "rollback" under docs/releases/v2 or scripts/release.

evidence.author: Nadia Chen
evidence.quote: REL-260: “Write v2 rollback runbook” is still in Backlog, unassigned.

resolutions.label: Write the runbook before launch
resolutions.description: Document and test rollback steps; assign an owner.

resolutions.label: Delegate to SRE
resolutions.description: Create a release-blocking ticket for the SRE team.

resolutions.label: Ship behind a feature flag
resolutions.description: Accept the risk with a documented flag-off path.
